learnings.claim: YouTube native title and thumbnail A/B test is not a Shorts experiment; Shorts packaging iteration must not be labeled as that product.
learnings.decision: Use sequential owned-channel metrics for Shorts experiments and reserve native A/B conclusions for eligible long-form only.
fallback_history: If native A/B eligibility is unclear, do not transfer the result to Shorts.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next Shorts analytics read use engaged views, retention, and AVD or APV rather than a native A/B result.
learnings.title: Native YouTube A/B tests do not cover Shorts

learnings.claim: When a YouTube Analytics report uses the video dimension or a video filter, subscribersGained and subscribersLost include only subscribe and unsubscribe actions from that video watch page, not channel page or home guide actions.
learnings.decision: SUBSCRIBER_CONVERSION_GATE: after analytics maturity, record subscribersGained, subscribersLost, net subscribers, engagedViews, and net subscribers per 1000 engaged views when the denominator is positive. Label the result watch-page-attributed. Do not score a Short on raw views alone and do not treat a video-filtered net as total channel subscriber change or Shorts-feed attribution.
failure_history: Commit b1a9ff76 added subscriber conversion code and tests but left learning_ledger.json without a SUBSCRIBER_CONVERSION_GATE row.
fallback_history: If an authorized video-filtered Analytics query is unavailable, keep subscriber conversion unknown and do not infer it from raw views or channel-level subscriber change.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized video-filtered Analytics read-back, store subscribersGained, subscribersLost, engagedViews, and the watch-page label. Do not invent numbers if the query fails.
learnings.title: Video-filtered subscriber metrics are watch-page only

learnings.claim: YouTube highlights intro, top-moment, spike and dip labels only when they are detected, and the video should be at least 60 seconds long and have at least 100 views. Audience retention data typically takes 1-2 days. A 25-30 second Short should not be expected to receive those highlighted labels even when video-level retention exists.
learnings.decision: KEY_MOMENTS_DURATION_GATE: for 25-30 second Shorts, do not wait for or require highlighted intro/top-moment/spike/dip labels. After processing, use available video-level retention plus stayed/chose-to-view, engaged views, AVD, APV and watch time. Classify missing highlighted labels on a sub-60-second Short as not_applicable_by_duration, not as an analytics failure.
failure_history: Markdown youtube-short-retention-key-moments-limit-2026-10-02 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If highlighted key moments are absent on a sub-60-second Short, classify as not_applicable_by_duration and use the available retention curve or metrics. If retention itself is missing before 1-2 days, mark immature rather than zero.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned Short after at least 1-2 days, record retention_available, processing age, stayed-to-watch, engaged views, AVD, APV and watch time. Do not score missing key-moment labels as a failure when duration is under 60 seconds.
learnings.title: Shorts under 60 seconds do not get highlighted retention key moments

learnings.claim: URLs in Shorts descriptions and comments are non-clickable; a Related video link can be clickable in the Shorts player when advanced-feature access and eligibility are verified.
learnings.decision: Do not design a conversion CTA that depends on a raw description or comment URL; prefer native Related video only after access read-back.
fallback_history: Use a separately verified clickable surface; do not infer clickability from plain text.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next suitable Short, verify advanced-feature access before using Related video and do not claim conversion lift without owned analytics.
learnings.title: Shorts description and comment URLs are not the clickable route

learnings.claim: Per-workflow concurrency groups prevent duplicate runs of one workflow but do not serialize different workflows that push to the same branch.
learnings.decision: Use one repo-main-writers group with queue max for all workflows that commit to main, while retaining pull-rebase as a secondary conflict check.
failure_history: Ten write-capable workflows used separate concurrency groups, allowing cross-workflow pushes to overlap.
fallback_history: If a queued run reaches the 100-run limit or stalls, stop the unhealthy writer and preserve the existing pull-rebase conflict path.
learnings.next_measurement: Verify workflow validation, successful CI, and the next scheduled writer runs without push conflicts or canceled pending jobs.
learnings.title: Repository writers need one queued concurrency group

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics supports insightPlaybackLocationType so views and estimated watch time can be grouped by the page or application where playback occurred. Playback location is not the same dimension as insightTrafficSourceType and does not by itself prove why a video performed.
learnings.decision: PLAYBACK_LOCATION_CONTEXT_GATE: when authorized mature Analytics is available, pair views and watch time with insightPlaybackLocationType, compare like-for-like contexts, and do not merge playback location with traffic source. If authorized data is missing, keep location unknown.
failure_history: Markdown learn_youtube_playback_location_context_20261003 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
fallback_history: If authorized playback-location data is unavailable, keep location unknown and use existing engagedViews, retention, and traffic-source evidence without guessing location.
learnings.next_measurement: After Analytics maturity on a real Short, retrieve insightPlaybackLocationType with views and estimatedMinutesWatched and record whether conclusions change when contexts are separated. Do not query before the 48-72 hour window.
learnings.title: Playback location is context, not traffic source or causality

learnings.claim: After the 2026-08-27 public view alignment, public views count from the first frame and must not be used as a substitute for engagedViews in quality or monetization comparisons.
learnings.decision: PUBLIC_VS_ENGAGED_VIEW_GATE: use public views for reach/start exposure and engagedViews plus AVD/APV/retention for quality; store metric name and definition date.
fallback_history: If engagedViews is unavailable, mark engaged performance unknown rather than substituting public views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized Short analytics read, fetch views and engagedViews for the same video and date window; do not infer engagedViews from public views.
learnings.title: Public views and engagedViews are not interchangeable after 2026-08-27

learnings.claim: YouTube Analytics API data is not real-time; processing typically adds 48-72 hours of latency, and responses omit recent days until all requested metrics are fully processed. Current per-video view, like, and comment counts belong to Data API videos.list, not Analytics.
learnings.decision: ANALYTICS_MATURITY_GATE: do not close retention or watch-time learning from Analytics API data before the documented processing window. Do not treat missing recent Analytics rows as zero. Use Data API or verified Studio state for current counts, then re-read Analytics after at least 72 hours.
failure_history: Markdown learning learn_youtube_analytics_latency_gate_20261002 was on main without a learning_ledger row, so the machine set could not discover it.
fallback_history: If authorized Analytics API is unavailable, use verified Studio analytics after sufficient processing time; otherwise mark the metric unknown and do not infer it from public views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized real Short, record publish time, a fast-state count where available, then Analytics after at least 72 hours. Only the mature read may close retention or watch-time learning.
learnings.title: Analytics API learning waits for the 48-72 hour processing window

learnings.claim: POSIX flock protects processes sharing one checkout, while GitHub Contents API updates require the current blob SHA and serialized remote writes.
learnings.decision: Keep local flock plus atomic replace; remote writers must read the current blob SHA, write serially, and re-read after conflicts.
failure_history: A local file lock cannot coordinate independent GitHub runners or automation branches.
fallback_history: On conflict, fetch the new blob SHA and reassess the delta before one bounded retry.
learnings.next_measurement: Track HTTP 409 or 422 conflicts and verify successful read-back on the merged main branch.
learnings.title: Local and remote write locks are separate

learnings.claim: Rights clearance is necessary but not sufficient for revenue-targeted Shorts; substantive original contribution is also required, and optional music can change Creator Pool allocation.
learnings.decision: Before publish require commercial rights clearance and a distinct originality or reused-content gate; evaluate music only when it adds narrative or retention value.
fallback_history: If rights or originality cannot be verified, replace with original or licensed footage and original narration.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next Shorts production decision record rights source, originality evidence, and whether music is used.
learnings.title: Shorts revenue needs originality plus rights, and music is not revenue-neutral

learnings.claim: Authorized YouTube Analytics can segment owned-video discovery by insightTrafficSourceType and, for supported sources, insightTrafficSourceDetail. Raw views do not establish feed, browse, or search mix.
learnings.decision: Before changing packaging or distribution, classify discovery source only from an authorized report. Otherwise mark traffic source unknown. Do not invent search terms or external pages.
failure_history: Markdown learning learn_youtube_traffic_source_feedback_loop_20261002 was absent from learning_ledger.json after the 18:30 write, so the machine set could not discover it.
fallback_history: If authorized Analytics or Studio read-back is unavailable, keep traffic source unknown and do not change packaging from raw views.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned Short with authorized Analytics, record insightTrafficSourceType and supported detail beside engaged views and retention. Do not infer source mix from raw views.
learnings.title: Traffic source must be classified before packaging changes

learnings.claim: From 24 August 2026 YouTube counts a view when playback starts, while Shorts earnings still use engaged views and YPP eligibility still uses qualified views.
learnings.decision: Annotate the counting change before comparing historical raw views and prioritize engaged views, watch time, and retention.
fallback_history: If Analytics access is unavailable, keep the methodology note and do not treat raw-view deltas as content-performance proof.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next owned-channel analytics read record whether engagedViews and retention metrics are available.
learnings.title: Post-August 2026 raw Shorts views are not comparable without a methodology note

learnings.claim: GitHub Apps should request only the minimum permissions needed; Contents and Workflows permissions are separate capabilities.
learnings.decision: For repository automation, grant Contents only when code/file access is required and add Workflows only when .github/workflows files must be edited.
failure_history: Treating a visible or installed GitHub App as proof of appropriately scoped access can overstate both capability and safety.
fallback_history: If the required permission cannot be confirmed, keep the integration available_unverified and use read-only/manual review instead of expanding access.
learnings.next_measurement: Compare the documented minimum with the actual installed app permissions when authorized account-level visibility is available.
learnings.title: Separate GitHub App Contents and Workflows permissions

learnings.claim: DEEP_ENGAGEMENT_GATE: when authorized mature Analytics data is available, evaluate shares and net playlist-add events (videosAddedToPlaylists minus videosRemovedFromPlaylists) alongside engagedViews, retention and subscriber conversion. Normalize per 1000 engaged views when the denominator is available. Playlist metrics are absolute event counts, include Watch Later, exclude automatic uploads/history lists, and are not unique viewers, purchases, or recommendation causality.
learnings.decision: CONSENSUS. Markdown on f536f50 was not a machine row. Official metrics page confirms shares, videosAddedToPlaylists and videosRemovedFromPlaylists definitions. Do not infer owned-channel values.
failure_history: No authorized channel Analytics call in this cycle.
fallback_history: If playlist metrics are unavailable, keep verified shares plus retention and subscriber gates; do not estimate.
learnings.next_measurement: On a mature owned Short, read engagedViews, shares, videosAddedToPlaylists and videosRemovedFromPlaylists for the same video and date window; store shares per 1000 engaged views and net playlist-add events per 1000 engaged views. If unavailable, mark unknown.
learnings.title: YouTube Shorts deep-engagement save/share gate

learnings.claim: Shopify product-bundles overview says bundles can sell on Online Store, Shop, POS, and Google and YouTube for fixed bundles only. The Shopify Bundles app page says channels other than Online Store or headless are unsupported, while its publish steps also name Shop and POS.
learnings.decision: CHANNEL_COMPATIBILITY_GATE: before recommending or activating a bundle, record target_sales_channel, bundle_type, and bundle_app. Do not publish when support is false or when official pages conflict; mark channel_support_unverified and keep draft. Google and YouTube stays fixed-bundle-only unless a newer official page supersedes it. Channel support is not a demand or margin signal.
failure_history: Markdown shopify-bundle-channel-compatibility-guard-2026-10-02 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
Overview page and Shopify Bundles app limitations page disagree on Shop and POS.
fallback_history: If official channel docs conflict or cannot be re-read, keep the candidate draft and do not infer support from app UI or search snippets.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next bundle candidate, record channel, bundle type, app, and whether the current official page pair agrees. No Admin publish.
learnings.title: Bundle channel support is page-specific and not assumed

learnings.claim: Eligible creators can tag products in Shorts and the first tagged product is the Shopping product sticker, reorderable, with size and position adjustable in the YouTube mobile app. Sticker visibility is not guaranteed. Auto-tag help page 17046000 was not found on 2026-10-02, so automatic tags must not be treated as currently documented. Shopping is not active for this channel until Studio read-back proves eligibility and store connection.
learnings.decision: SHOPPING_PRODUCT_STICKER_GATE: on a product-led Short, prefer a reviewed native product tag and explicit first/featured product only after eligibility and store connection are read back. Preserve safe visual space. Do not treat a raw Shorts URL as the conversion path. If Shopping is unavailable, use the verified Related-video routing fallback.
failure_history: Markdown learn_youtube_shopping_shorts_product_sticker_20261002 was on main without a learning_ledger row.
https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/17046000 returned not found on 2026-10-02, so auto-tag is not a verified current source.
fallback_history: If Shopping eligibility or store connection is unproven, do not claim Shopping is active; use verified same-channel Related video routing and do not rely on raw Shorts description or comment URLs.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized product-led Short, read back Shopping eligibility and store connection, tag the exact product, confirm it is first, inspect mobile sticker placement, and record clicks only when analytics are mature.
learnings.title: Shorts Shopping sticker is capability, not channel proof

learnings.claim: YouTube Reporting API device_type values are 100 unknown, 101 computer, 102 TV, 103 game console, 104 mobile phone and 105 tablet, with operating_system as a separate dimension. channel_device_os_a3 segments by device_type and operating_system. channel_combined_a3 documents playback_location_type, traffic_source_type, device_type and operating_system together as a Reporting API bulk schema. That documented bulk schema is not a license to invent an Analytics API query combination, and no authorized channel device query was run, so device mix remains unknown and is not algorithmic causality.
learnings.decision: DEVICE_CONTEXT_GATE: when authorized data exists, segment engaged views and watch time with a documented device or device/OS report before interpreting format performance. Use channel_combined_a3 only as a Reporting API bulk job, not as an assumed Analytics API cross-join. If device data is unavailable, mark device context unknown and do not infer it from public views.
failure_history: Commit 45d9252 added knowledge/2026-10-03-youtube-device-context-gate.md only. learning_ledger.json had no DEVICE_CONTEXT_GATE row on read-back.
fallback_history: If authorized device data is unavailable, keep engagedViews, retention, traffic source and playback location layers and mark device context unknown.
learnings.next_measurement: On the next authorized Reporting or Analytics read-back, request a documented device_type or device/OS report and store engaged views and watch time by device. Do not invent numbers if the job fails.
learnings.title: Device context is a supported segmentation layer, not channel proof

learnings.claim: Shopify Analytics session measurement rolled out 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-23. Sessions follow continued activity and end after 30 minutes of inactivity instead of always splitting at midnight UTC. Some sessions without a pageview are counted. Identified bot sessions are filtered from session reports by default. Conversion rate and other session-derived metrics can move even when orders, sales and customer counts do not. Historical data is not reprocessed; post-update session data is a new baseline. Bot classification applies only to sessions from 2025-10-07 onward.
learnings.decision: SESSION_MEASUREMENT_BASELINE_GUARD: timestamp the Shopify metric definition. Do not interpret a boundary jump in sessions, conversion rate, add-to-cart rate, reached-checkout rate, checkout conversion rate, bounce rate, pageviews per session, average session duration or online-store visitors across 2026-09-21..23 as demand change by itself. Cross-check orders, sales and customer counts. Compare post-update periods with the same human/bot filter where that filter exists. If metric version or filter state is unknown, mark the session-derived comparison non-comparable.
failure_history: Commit 158be857 added the guard only to knowledge/lessons.md. learning_ledger.json and source_catalog.json had no matching row on read-back.
fallback_history: If session metric version or human/bot filter state is unknown, do not compare session-derived rates and fall back to orders, sales and customer counts plus a post-update baseline.
learnings.next_measurement: After the store is public and an authorized Analytics read exists, compare only post-2026-09-23 like-for-like periods with the same human/bot filter, and record orders, sales and customers beside sessions. Do not invent store numbers.
learnings.title: Shopify session metrics need a post-2026-09-23 baseline
